turns.text: 2:12 am update. just finished the feed, theo is back down, typing one-handed sorry. short version please: what are typical wake windows and nap lengths for a 4 month old? i want to compare to the log

Short version for about 4 months:

- Wake windows: roughly 75-120 minutes
- Naps per day: 3-4
- Nap length: 30 minutes to 2 hours, with lots of variation
- Total daytime sleep: about 3-5 hours
- Nighttime sleep: about 10-12 hours, usually with a feed or two

Every baby falls somewhere in these ranges, so treat them as guides, not targets. Want me to put it in a table?
yes please, table form, with ranges. i want to chart his actual wake windows against the numbers. he takes three crib naps around 9, 12:30 and 4 with 90 minute wake windows. does that match norms

| Measure | Typical range at ~4 months | Your numbers |
|---|---|---|
| Wake window | 75-120 min | 90 min (middle of range) |
| Naps per day | 3-4 | 3 (in range) |
| Nap length | 30 min-2 hrs | check the log |
| Daytime sleep total | 3-5 hrs | add up the three naps |
| Nap spacing | every 1.5-2 hrs awake | 9, 12:30, 4 fits that |

Three crib naps with 90-minute wake windows is right in the typical zone. Some babies this age drop to 2 longer naps or add a short fourth, but there's nothing to fix if he's content between naps.

For charting: plot each wake window as a bar with the 75-120 shaded band behind it, and flag any nap under 30 minutes.

nice. one more thing, the log shows a 40 minute stroller nap yesterday... wait no friday was the storm. anyway he conked out for 40 minutes in the stroller after laps at delgado park. do stroller naps count toward the total? scoreboard says dad confused

Yes, they count. Sleep is sleep, and a 40-minute stroller nap counts toward his daytime total and resets his wake window like any other nap.

Things to know:
- Motion naps are often lighter, so they can leave a baby a little less rested than the same time in a crib.
- If a stroller nap lands near a crib nap, it can shorten the next wake window a bit.
- Log it as its own row with a note ("stroller") so you can compare it against crib naps in your chart.

If he's happy and his schedule holds, one stroller nap now and then is fine.
perfect, adding a stroller column to the table now. thanks
Sounds good. A "location" column (crib or stroller) will make it easy to see patterns. Hope he sleeps well for the rest of the night, and you do too.
